notes: Key pain: refunds processing is manual -> ops cost + refunds errors during promo spikes
Customer quote on call: 'We need the bot to do the right thing 99.9% — a bad refund is expensive.'
Primary integration: internal refunds microservice (REST) + payments gateway (tokenized charges).
They require tool-calling to create/update refund tickets, trigger refunds, and escalate to ops with context (charge id, risk score, policy id).
POC scope: agent-assist UI snippets, automated ticket summaries, and idempotent refund API calls with audit trail.
Requested features: function/tool calling with deterministic outputs, structured JSON responses for downstream systems, and an audit log that ties model outputs to request ids.
Operational constraints: burst-safe routing during sales peaks (x20 traffic on Black Friday-like events), no silent failures — fallbacks to read-only mode or human-in-the-loop required.
Security asks: bring-your-own-key (KMS/HSM), SSO for console, retention controls for PII, SOC2 attestation is mandatory; potential ISO discussion later.

Legal wants a specific addendum around PCI scope and certs before Prod sign-off.
They plan to start with Dedicated in VPC for pilot, then evaluate Private (on-prem) for largest enterprise customers requiring air-gapped processing of cardholder data.
requirements_summary: Workload: mixed - agent assist for CS reps (low-latency), bulk ticket summarization (throughput), automated refunds (transactional, idempotent tool-calls)
Latency targets: agent assist sub-200ms prefer for token latency, 95th <= 400ms; ticket summarization can be async (batch within 30s)
Throughput: baseline 500 reqs/min with ability to scale to 10k reqs/min for promo spikes
Reliability: strict SLAs during spikes; fallback policies to alternate model or manual queueing
Model preferences: small-to-medium LLM for deterministic tool-calling + stronger models for summarization; model variant pinning required
Routing/fallback: route primary to dedicated low-latency pool, fallback to lower-cost region or hosted variant when capacity constrained
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, per-request audit id linking to refund transactions
Integration: webhook-based tool calling, signed JWTs for service-to-service calls, and idempotency keys
Compliance: must demonstrate audit logs mapping model output -> ticket id -> refunded charge; retention controls to purge PII on request
